10.0.0.en: 1- "Why standest thou afar off, O Lord? Why hidest thou thyself in times of trouble?"

10.0.1.en: 1- David describes his feeling in affliction, which is that he does not sense God near to him, as though He had hidden Himself, although he trusts in His presence and nearness. But the feeling of affliction envelops a person and covers him, just as Christ on the Cross felt, as man, the severity of affliction and pain and the distance of God from Him, though He is God united with man. He expressed this affliction by saying, "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?" (Mt 27:46).

10.0.2.en: 2- The feeling that God is far from a person in the midst of affliction may be because the person has distanced himself from God, and not the reverse. But whoever continues in prayer and crying out, like David, will surely feel God's nearness to him, as David expressed this in the same psalm in (v. 17).

10.0.3.en: 3- God sometimes leaves a person for a time in the midst of affliction, not out of neglect, but to stir his feelings so that he cries out to God and receives greater blessings. In this way God tests his faith and blesses him with abundant blessings.

10.0.4.en: 4- A person's feeling in afflictions that God is far from him makes him not only cry out to Him, but also leave his lusts and sins and renounce the world, so that he is purified from evil and filled with the grace of God.

10.0.5.en: Let the affliction you pass through be a motive for you to much prayer and crying out to God, so that you grow spiritually and experience new depths in the love of God.

10.1.0.en: 2- "In the pride of the wicked the poor is burned; they are taken in the plot that they have devised."

10.1.1.en: 1- The wicked man is full of evil thoughts and deeds, and in pride he persists in his evil to harm the poor and try to destroy him; that is, the wicked man has neither compassion nor love.

10.1.2.en: 2- God allows the evil of the wicked only to the extent that benefits the poor. But He makes the evil of the wicked come upon his own head and his plots harm himself, as this meaning was confirmed in (Ps 7:15, 16; Ps 9:15). This meaning is repeated often in the Holy Bible, such as Babylon, which brought down many and was utterly destroyed, as the Book of Revelation tells us (Rev 17:5, 6; 18:6), and Ahab, who wronged Naboth, and the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, so the dogs also licked the blood of Ahab, as Elijah had told him (1 Kgs 21:19).

10.1.3.en: 3- God disciplines the wicked by making his evil come upon his own head, to declare that evil is hateful before Him and that He does not want any of His children to walk in it; for evil binds its owner and keeps him away from God, from the good, and from every good work, and he becomes like a blind man who sees nothing but evil, just as the blind man sees nothing but darkness.

10.1.4.en: 4- The wicked man seizes the opportunity of God's hiddenness in times of trouble, as (v. 1) mentions, and persists in his evil in pride. But God is longsuffering and gives him an opportunity to review himself; yet if he does not benefit from this opportunity, He turns his evil upon his own head.

10.1.5.en: 5- David the poor man calls upon God and cries to Him for help, that He may save him and save all the poor who are burned by the evil of the wicked, and he asks for their deliverance. Of course God hastens to His children and does not neglect them, especially since the faith of some of them may be shaken and they doubt the swiftness of God's answer and support, so that they burn inwardly with these doubts, and so they need swift divine help.

10.2.0.en: 3- "For the wicked boasteth of the desires of his soul, and the robber blasphemeth. He despiseth the Lord."

10.2.1.en: 1- Here he mentions a second characteristic of the wicked man after pride, which is lust. The wicked man is immersed in bodily lusts and persists in them until he justifies these evil lusts, so that his persistence in them increases, and he reaches the point of boasting of them, and consequently advances in them without limit.

10.2.2.en: 2- The wicked man's boasting of his lusts increases his pride, and he is often glorified by people, which increases his persistence in lust; because in his sight God is hidden in times of trouble, and people think that the wicked man is right, while the godly are poor and weak; that is, concepts and principles are turned upside down.

10.2.3.en: 3- Those who praise him may be hypocrites seeking their own interest and benefit, but the wicked man is deceived by these words, so his pride increases, and in his lusts he falls also into another, third sin, which is greed. He seizes from others, that is, he steals, and it may be a forced theft, using his power and influence.

10.2.4.en: 4- Through the wicked man's greed he falls into a fourth sin, which is injustice; he assaults the property of others and seizes their rights to satisfy his selfishness.

10.2.5.en: 5- Then the wicked robber goes further and falls into a fifth sin, which is blasphemy against God, since he feels his power and authority over others through what he takes from them, so he insults God and describes Him with evil attributes, because he relies on his own strength in pride, neglects God's commandments, and feels no need of God, so he stands as an equal against God and blasphemes Him.

10.3.0.en: 4- "The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, saith: He will not require it. All his thoughts are that there is no God."

10.3.1.en: 1- The sixth sin of the wicked man is atheism; for in his pride and loftiness he says of God that He does not require it, and even says there is no God.

10.3.2.en: 2- The cause of atheism is falling into the sin of pride, lust and greed, so that in his loftiness he lifts his nose above all who are around him, despising others; that is, he feels that with a puff of his nose he can destroy others, meaning that with a little strength of his he destroys the poor. Therefore he feels no need for the existence of God and abolishes His existence.

10.3.3.en: 3- The wicked man's fall into atheism comes gradually; as he becomes great in his own eyes and domineers over others, he forgets God, then he grows insolent and describes God as weak and passive, because He will not demand the rights of the poor, as proved by the fact that he has been lording it over the poor for a period of time and God has not punished him. And in the end he reaches atheism by rejecting the idea of God's existence, so that he may persist in his evil without limit.

10.3.4.en: 4- God rebukes a person and warns him many times to return, and when God's anger against the person increases, He abandons him, so that he may suffer the consequences of his sins and be pricked, perhaps he will repent, as it says of the wicked in the Epistle to the Romans, "God gave them over to a reprobate mind" (Rom 1:28).

10.3.5.en: 5- The wicked man in his evil assaults people with injustice, contempt and domination. Then he goes further in his insolence to assault God Himself, and blasphemes Him, and in the end claims that God does not exist; that is, he falls into atheism.

10.3.6.en: 6- Behind atheism stand not only lusts but also man's deification of himself, and in the end he falls into atheism, and this is what the Antichrist will fall into.

10.4.0.en: 5- "His ways are always grievous; thy judgments are far above out of his sight: as for all his enemies, he puffeth at them."

10.4.1.en: Puffeth: blows, and what is meant is that he pours out his venom, his authority and his evil upon his enemies.

10.4.2.en: 1- The wicked man lives in his uncleanness and evils and is firm in his evil ways, since he silences his conscience and justifies his faults, so he persists in his sins.

10.4.3.en: 2- As the wicked man is immersed in evil and becomes accustomed to it, God becomes far from his mind and heart, and His commandments become high above him, which he cannot grasp, and he gives them no weight, so he neglects them completely.

10.4.4.en: 3- Since the wicked man has put God away from his thinking and has become accustomed to evil, he directs his evils against the godly and the poor, so he harms them and regards them as his enemies, because by their righteousness they expose his evil; therefore he tries to crush them.

10.4.5.en: 4- We see here a clear relationship between uncleanness and evil on the one hand, and the rejection of God and atheism on the other; the wicked man rejects the existence of God so that he may persist in his evil and no one may rebuke him for it.

10.5.0.en: 6- "He hath said in his heart: I shall not be moved: for I shall never be in adversity."

10.5.1.en: When the wicked man persists in his evil he feels strong and secure, relying on material things, so he thinks to himself that no one can shake him or harm him; he deludes himself with security and happiness, although he knows that the whole world is changeable and that evil passes away, but he forgets reality and lives in illusions, that is, he lives an imaginary happiness although his heart is troubled within him, like the foolish rich man who trusted in his wealth, but was surprised that he would die that very night (Lk 12:19, 20).

10.6.0.en: 7- "His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and fraud: under his tongue is mischief and vanity."

10.6.1.en: 1- The seventh characteristic of the wicked man is abuse; he is not content with blaspheming God, but curses and reviles the righteous who expose his evil by their righteousness. He does not repent, but on the contrary curses righteousness and the righteous.

10.6.2.en: 2- The eighth characteristic is deceit; for the wicked man cheats those around him to reach his evil goals, and he is also a hypocrite and a pretender, so he speaks sweet words by which he deceives those around him and makes them imagine that evil is delightful and gives happiness, while he carries under his tongue, that is, he hides, the toil and torment that evil contains; whoever is deceived by the pleasure of sin suffers afterward from its troubles.

10.6.3.en: 3- The sweet tongue of the wicked man may be in spiritual speech, but he hides under it innovations and heresies; his evil does not appear on his tongue but under it, to deceive by it the poor and the simple if they stray from God.

10.7.0.en: 8- "He sitteth in the lurking places of the villages: in the secret places doth he murder the innocent: his eyes are privily set against the poor. 9- He lieth in wait secretly as a lion in his den: he lieth in wait to catch the poor: he doth catch the poor, when he draweth him into his net." Lurking place: an ambush, a place where the wicked man hides to pounce on the innocent and destroy them. His den: the house of the lion.

10.7.1.en: 1- The wicked man is characterized not only by deceit but also by violence, which is the ninth characteristic of the wicked man; he hides quietly so that the poor man scarcely suspects him, and suddenly he comes out of the ambush in which he was hiding to pounce on the poor man and devour him.

10.7.2.en: 2- The wicked man watches the righteous not to learn righteousness from them or to care for them, but on the contrary to seize an opportunity and harm them, and if possible destroy them. His looks, his words and his deeds are all evil.

10.7.3.en: 3- He cannot harm the righteous, because God protects them and does not allow harm to come to them except what benefits them spiritually, as happened with the martyrs. But the wicked man can seize the opportunity of the weakness of the righteous and make them fall into sin; therefore the children of God must constantly hold fast to His commandments and examine themselves every day.

10.7.4.en: 4- This verse likens the wicked man to a ravening lion, that is, extreme violence and at the same time trickery, like the hunter who casts his net so that the innocent fall into it. This is what happened with the Church, which was and is exposed to the cruelty of persecution and also to the deception of heretics.

10.8.0.en: 10- "So he is crushed, and bowed down, and the poor fall by his strong ones." (literally: the poor fall in his claws).

10.8.2.en: 1- Before the cruelty of the wicked man the righteous grow weary, carrying their cross for the sake of Christ, so they are crushed and bowed down to the ground under the weight of the cross, and even offer their lives as a sacrifice of the love of God.

10.8.3.en: 2- Of the righteous, whoever grows careless and looks to earthly lusts, bending over them, the wicked man seizes this opportunity and makes them fall into sin, crushes them, and sinks his claws into them and destroys them. This wicked man is Satan and all the wicked who follow him, such as the Antichrist who comes at the end of days.

10.9.0.en: 11- "He hath said in his heart: God hath forgotten: he hideth his face; he will never see it."

10.9.1.en: So that the wicked man may persist in his evil, he imagines and claims either that God does not exist, or that He is weak, so he accuses Him of forgetting and being occupied with something other than His weak children, and even that He will not turn to their prayers and their crying out to Him, and will remain far from them forever. In this way the wicked man numbs his conscience, because he cannot bear to remember the great punishment of judgment.

10.9.2.en: If a person accepts doing evil, or thinking about it even a little, evil creeps into his life, grows and gains control over him, so he justifies his faults and assaults God with evil words. So be careful to repent, that you may reject sin first by first, and return to God and gain the salvation of your soul.

10.10.0.en: 12- "Arise, O Lord; O God, lift up thine hand: forget not the poor."

10.10.1.en: 1- David calls upon God to end His longsuffering and forbearance toward the wicked, so that He may rescue His poor children and punish the wicked with the power of His hand, that is, with His divine might.

10.10.2.en: 2- The hand of God is a type of His Incarnation; David, in the spirit of prophecy, calls upon Christ to rise from the dead, binding the power of Satan and rescuing His poor servants who believe in Him from the dominion of the devil.

10.10.3.en: 3- David also awaits the rising of Christ on the Day of Judgment, to judge the wicked and glorify His righteous children who endured much on earth, so that they receive in return for it blessings in the Kingdom of Heaven.

10.11.0.en: 13- "Wherefore doth the wicked contemn God? He hath said in his heart: Thou wilt not require it."

10.11.1.en: David the prophet denounces the wicked man's contempt for God and his claim that God will judge no one; this is considered a denial of God's existence and authority, and therefore he is severely punished by God.

10.12.0.en: 14- "Thou hast seen it; for thou beholdest mischief and spite, to requite it with thy hand: the poor committeth himself unto thee; thou art the helper of the fatherless."

10.12.1.en: 1- David proclaims the truth against the claims of the wicked, so he addresses God and says to Him: You have seen the evil of the wicked and their injustice, and You have felt the troubles of Your poor children and their toil. And You are a tender Father who cannot bear injustice to Your children; as happened in ancient times when God had compassion on His people in Egypt, humiliated in the slavery of Pharaoh, and looked upon their toil and declared to Moses that He would come down and deliver them (Ex 18:8).

10.12.2.en: 2- He declares that God will requite the wicked and punish them for their injustice to the poor, as He punished the nations that humiliated His people, such as Egypt, Assyria and Babylon.

10.12.3.en: 3- The strong hand of God that punishes the wicked is the very hand on which the hope of His children depends, when they feel that they are poor and weak, and even fatherless, that is, without earthly father and mother to support them, so that You, O God, are a Father to them and a helper in their hardships.

10.12.4.en: Do not be troubled if you feel that you are alone, or weak before the powers of the world, or the wars of Satan, for God loves the weak and supports them. Take refuge in Him, confident of His power that saves you from every evil.

10.13.0.en: 15- "Break thou the arm of the wicked and the evil man: seek out his wickedness till thou find none."

10.13.2.en: 1- David asks God to break the arm, that is, the power, of the wicked man, so that he may feel his weakness before God and his helplessness; he does not gloat over the wicked man or try to take vengeance on him, but wants the breaking of evil, so that the wicked may repent.

10.13.3.en: 2- When God breaks the power of evil the wicked man can do nothing, and his works are of no use or effect upon the righteous poor, because God protects them; this strengthens the faith of the poor in God and calls the wicked man to repentance.

10.13.4.en: 3- God's breaking of the power of evil is completed on the great Day of Judgment, when the devil and all his followers are judged, and in the Kingdom of Heaven they have no power, but the righteous poor live in perfect happiness with God.

10.14.0.en: 16- "The Lord is King for ever and ever: the heathen are perished out of his land."

10.14.1.en: 1- God reassures His children that He is King over His people and the hearts of His children, so He protects them from every evil, and even destroys the enemies, that is, the nations, from their land. But He says "his land", that is, He declares that the land of His people is His land and that He is responsible for them, which increases their reassurance.

10.14.2.en: 2- If God is King over the hearts of His children and protects them, He also gives them the enjoyment of fellowship with Him, so that they are distinguished from the rest of mankind by the fellowship of God.

10.14.3.en: 3- God is not only King now over His people, but also for ever and ever; He continues to give them enjoyment of His love and glory in complete stability, which increases and develops their joy.

10.14.4.en: 4- The land is a symbol of the heart of man, and the nations are a symbol of sins; so when God reigns over His land, that is, the heart of His son and beloved who has believed in Him, He removes sins from him and helps him to destroy them, so that the whole heart may be God's, fulfilling the commandment that says, "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart" (Mt 22:37).

10.14.5.en: 5- The land is also a symbol of the Kingdom of Heaven, and the nations are a symbol of the demons and the wicked who have no place in the Kingdom, and thus the children of God enjoy perpetual joy with God, without the presence of the wicked with them.

10.15.0.en: 17- "Lord, thou hast heard the desire of the humble: thou wilt prepare their heart, thou wilt cause thine ear to hear." (literally: the groaning of the meek you have heard, O Lord; you establish their hearts; you incline your ear)

10.15.1.en: 1- The sufferings of the godly believers who live in meekness and quietness are very precious to God; not only does their crying out move Him, but their mere groaning makes Him hasten to hear them and answer them.

10.15.2.en: 2- God's swift intervention and His condescension to incline His ear to them reassures the meek and gives them inner steadfastness and stability, so that they are no longer disturbed by outward afflictions, even if these continue for a time, but He gives them blessing, spiritual depth and inward delight during the affliction.

10.15.3.en: 3- God's hearing of the groaning of the meek, who ask for His justice and equity for them in the face of the injustice of the wicked, is completed in the Kingdom of Heaven when He glorifies them with Him for ever, and punishes the wicked in eternal torment.

10.15.4.en: 4- The meek in the Old Testament groaned to God to deliver them from the cruelty of the devil, so He became incarnate in the fullness of time and bound Satan by His Cross, and brought Adam and his children up from Hades to Paradise.

10.16.0.en: 18- "To judge the fatherless and the oppressed, that the man of the earth may no more oppress."

10.16.1.en: 1- God moves by His justice to do right and restore the rights of two groups:

10.16.2.en: a - The fatherless, that is, those without support and care, or those whom sin has deprived of their strength and who repent, so God becomes a Father to them and cares for them with His providence.

10.16.3.en: b - The oppressed, that is, the humble who seek God, so He rescues them, restores their rights to them and distinguishes them from others.

10.16.4.en: 2- God gives His children their spiritual rights before their material ones, because inner peace and the relationship with God are the most important, and He gives them strength to face outward problems, and then in the end He gives them their distinguished right in the Kingdom of Heaven.

10.16.5.en: 3- God's intervention frightens the enemies of His children, so they no longer terrify them and trouble them when they see God protecting them by His power. This is what happened with the saints, when Satan was afraid to come near their places and be burned by their prayers.

10.16.6.en: 4- When the children of God see His punishment of the wicked, not only are they reassured, but they also fear God, so their repentance and their care for their spiritual life increase.

10.16.7.en: Faith and steadfastness. For the choir director. Of David. "In the Lord I put my trust"... (v. 1). Introduction:

10.16.8.en: 1- Its writer: David the prophet, during Saul's pursuit of him, when the wicked frightened him and asked him to hide in the mountains so that Saul would forget him, but he preferred to trust in God and to be among his people and with his loved ones in the cities and villages.

10.16.9.en: 2- This psalm is considered a hymn of steadfastness in God during afflictions, so that a person is not shaken, whatever evils surround him. It also applies to the whole Church, when it is exposed to persecutions, and stands firm in faith in God.

10.16.10.en: 3- This psalm is among the psalms of faith, which call a person to faith in God and not to trust in the world and material things, and like it are Psalms (Ps 16, 23, 62, 125, 131).

10.16.11.en: 4- In this psalm the providence of God for the world appears; He cares for His children and watches all their works in order to care for them, and examines them to purify them from evil, but the wicked He punishes severely because of their disobedience and rebellion against Him.

10.16.12.en: 5- This psalm is not found in the Agpeya.
